audit_findings.title: Convertible notes are treated simultaneously as debt and equity
audit_findings.magnitude: 9.591 million conversion shares, 11.0% of the 87.487 million-share denominator; $219.518 million carrying debt and $382.8 million filed fair value
audit_findings.mechanism: The conversion shares enlarge the per-share denominator while note interest remains in OE and the possible cash settlement claim is unresolved in the bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: The 2030 Notes are convertible into solely cash, or a combination of cash and shares of common stock, at the Company’s election, at an initial conversion rate of 42.6257 shares of common stock per $1,000 principal amount of 2030 Notes, which is equivalent to an initial conversion price of $ 23.46003 per share of common stock.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated internal inconsistency. Holding the $800 million base equity value unchanged, removing the 9.591 million conversion shares would raise base value from $9.14 to approximately $10.27 per share. That denominator effect understates value, while failure to recognize the cash component of settlement could overstate value. The notes were already optionally convertible during the third quarter of 2026, making the settlement assumption current rather than remote.
audit_findings.action: Rerun cash-settlement and cash-plus-shares cases using one consistent treatment of conversion shares, cash paid, extinguished interest, issuance-cost amortization and any make-whole adjustment; probability-weight them if no single settlement policy can be established.

audit_findings.title: FY2025 contains only a partial year of the new financing cost
audit_findings.magnitude: $6.1 million FY2025 interest expense versus a $7.6 million annualized run rate from $3.8 million in first-half 2026; $1.5 million pretax gap
audit_findings.mechanism: An understated recurring financing expense raises the FY2025 OE anchor and every projected OE year if the notes remain debt.
audit_findings.evidence: In March 2025, the Company issued $ 225.0 million aggregate principal amount of 2.75 % Convertible Senior Notes due 2030 (the “2030 Notes”).
audit_findings.explanation: The partial-year mismatch is demonstrated, but its scale cannot change the valuation conclusion. Even treating the entire $1.5 million pretax gap as a dollar-for-dollar OE reduction would reduce base operating PV by approximately $21.1 million, base equity value by 2.6%, and base value by about $0.24 per share, leaving it near $8.90 versus the $24.59 market price.
audit_findings.action: If the debt case is retained, replace FY2025 note expense with the filed first-half 2026 run rate, including coupon and issuance-cost amortization, and apply the appropriate tax effect.

audit_findings.title: The FY2025 anchor may already be stale relative to known 2026 spending
audit_findings.magnitude: R&D increased $8.015 million, or 24.9%, in first-half 2026; operating income increased $2.934 million while operating cash flow decreased $8.038 million; OE impact unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Higher recurring R&D can lower near-term OE and alter the growth path, while contemporaneous revenue and gross-profit growth can offset that spending.
audit_findings.evidence: For 2026, we expect research and development expenses to increase from 2025 levels reflecting strategic investments in our growth priorities, including cybersecurity technology and AI technologies.
audit_findings.explanation: The spending increase is now demonstrated rather than merely forecast: first-half R&D rose to $40.171 million from $32.156 million. However, first-half operating income also increased, while operating cash flow declined because of working-capital movements. The supplied record therefore cannot establish whether a 2026-normalized OE anchor is above or below $31.5 million or whether the net difference is material.
audit_findings.action: Build trailing-twelve-month OE through June 2026 from the quarterly statements, separating recurring R&D, acquisition costs, interest income, note expense, stock compensation, capital expenditure and working-capital movements; rerun all scenarios from that reconciled anchor.

audit_findings.title: The entire cash and securities balance may not be distributable surplus
audit_findings.magnitude: $357.348 million cash and marketable securities added to the bridge, equal to 44.7% of $800 million base equity value; $154.826 million deferred revenue, including $93.230 million current; required adjustment unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Non-excess operating liquidity and cash associated with unperformed customer obligations should not be added as freely distributable value if the forecast also captures earnings from satisfying those obligations.
audit_findings.evidence: Deferred revenue primarily consists of amounts that have been invoiced but not yet recognized as revenue and consists of performance obligations pertaining to support and subscription services.
audit_findings.explanation: The model demonstrably adds the full liquid-asset balance, and the company simultaneously carries substantial deferred revenue. Deferred revenue is not deductible dollar-for-dollar because only fulfillment costs and cash-free runoff affect value, but the absence of any minimum-liquidity or runoff analysis leaves a bridge component representing nearly half of base equity value unsupported. That is reasonably capable of materially changing the valuation.
audit_findings.action: Prepare an excess-cash schedule that deducts minimum operating liquidity and models the revenue, fulfillment costs, deferred commissions and working-capital runoff tied to the opening $154.826 million deferred-revenue balance; rerun the bridge using only demonstrated surplus cash.

audit_findings.title: The latest OE anchor contains a favorable working-capital timing benefit
audit_findings.magnitude: $5.0 million favorable FY2025 working-capital change, 15.9% of the $31.5 million anchor; removing it dollar-for-dollar would reduce base operating PV by approximately $70.3 million and base value by approximately $0.80 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: A temporary working-capital release raises the OE anchor and is compounded through every forecast year and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: During the year ended December 31, 2025, cash provided by operating activities was $84.9 million, consisting of net income of $42.1 million, non-cash benefits totaling $37.8 million and a favorable net change in operating assets and liabilities of $5.0 million.
audit_findings.explanation: The $5.0 million FY2025 benefit is filed and explicitly attributed partly to collection and payment timing. Because the model grows the latest actual, this timing benefit can become a permanent modeled earning level. A dollar-for-dollar normalization would reduce base equity value by approximately 8.8%, from about $9.14 to $8.34 per share. First-half 2026 then recorded a $13.9 million adverse net working-capital movement, reinforcing that the FY2025 benefit was not a stable annual contribution, although that later movement may also contain timing effects.
audit_findings.action: Normalize receivables, inventory, payables, accrued liabilities, deferred revenue and deferred commissions using multi-year turnover or revenue relationships, then rerun all scenarios with the normalized working-capital requirement.

audit_findings.title: A disclosed one-time impairment appears retained in the latest-actual anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: $0.951 million, 3.0% of the $31.5 million anchor; a full dollar-for-dollar add-back would increase base value by approximately $0.15 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: If retained in OE despite being nonrecurring, the impairment lowers the anchor and all projected OE; if already excluded as a noncash item, there is no valuation effect.
audit_findings.evidence: Additionally, cost of services revenue includes a one-time asset impairment cost of $951 thousand for the year ended December 31, 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: The possible effect is too small to change the valuation conclusion. Even a full $0.951 million add-back would increase base operating PV by only about $13.4 million and base value from approximately $9.14 to $9.29 per share, still far below $24.59. Moreover, filed software impairments of approximately $0.9 million in 2024 and $3.0 million in 2023 indicate that abandoned development has recurred, and the record does not establish that the charge was actually retained in the OE calculation.
audit_findings.action: Trace the $0.951 million noncash charge through the FY2025 OE reconciliation and review prior software-project impairments; make no adjustment unless it both remains in OE and is demonstrably exceptional.
